sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Hackensack, NJ?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept a cash offer, and in Hackensack the right choice depends mostly on the house's condition and how soon you need to close. Hackensack is the county seat of Bergen County and its most populous municipality, with 46,030 residents in the 2020 census and a Census Bureau estimate of 46,380 for July 1, 2025.

Only 36.6 percent of Hackensack homes are owner-occupied, so a large share of the housing stock is rented. A seller of a two-family house or a small building should expect to deal with tenants, leases and rent questions as part of the sale. A cash buyer can shorten the calendar because no lender appraisal stands in the way, while the fire certificate, the tax payoff and the deed recording described below apply to every kind of sale.

sections.h2: What is Hackensack like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Hackensack covers 4.35 square miles roughly 12 miles northwest of Midtown Manhattan, and it fits several housing types into that space. The city's Wikipedia entry describes a residential high-rise district about a mile long on Prospect Avenue, suburban single-family streets that make up about one-third of the city (mostly on the west side), older two-family blocks, large garden apartment complexes and a small-city downtown.

Hackensack University Medical Center, the Bergen County Court House, the Metropolitan Campus of Fairleigh Dickinson University and a Bergen Community College location all sit in or beside the city. The neighbors are Bogota, Hasbrouck Heights, Little Ferry, Lodi, Maywood, Paramus, Ridgefield Park, River Edge, South Hackensack, Teaneck and Teterboro.

  • Single-family houses on the west side, including some older homes on lots of an acre or more.
  • Two-family houses in the older neighborhoods nearer the center.
  • Garden apartment complexes and the Prospect Avenue high-rises.
  • Mixed-use buildings in the downtown and the smaller neighborhood business districts.

sections.h2: Which inspection does Hackensack require before a house sale?
sections.html:
Hackensack's Fire Prevention Bureau issues a Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm and Portable Fire Extinguisher Compliance, and a seller needs it before the house changes hands. The city's form lists a $70 fee, says the certificate is valid for six months and says it is issued at the time of inspection.

A failed inspection or a missed appointment means a new application and another fee. The form asks for the buyer's name, the seller's name and the real estate company, and the city warns that incorrect information voids the report, so fill it out completely.

The rule comes from the state. New Jersey's Uniform Fire Code requires a smoke alarm certificate before any one-family or two-family dwelling is sold, leased or changes occupants, and the owner can obtain it only through the municipality. Get the equipment right first:

  • Smoke alarms on every floor including the basement, in common stairwells and hallways, and within 10 feet of each sleeping area.
  • Ten-year sealed battery alarms, which the Division of Fire Safety recommends replacing every 10 years.
  • A carbon monoxide alarm and a portable fire extinguisher, both named on the city form.

Ask the Building, Housing and Land Use department whether any further resale paperwork applies to your property type before you list.

sections.h2: How do Hackensack property taxes work when I sell?
sections.html:
Hackensack bills property tax in four installments due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, each with a 10-day grace period. Interest runs at 8 percent a year on the first $1,500 owed and 18 percent a year on anything above that. The tax collector's page says all taxes and charges must be current by November 10 or they enter the accelerated tax sale process that begins November 11.

The same page lists a 2026 final rate of $3.530 per $100 and says the 2026 final bills were mailed on September 16, 2026. It also warns new owners that the county may take three to six months to record a deed and pass the ownership change to the city, so a buyer should send the collector a mailing address right after closing. Ask the tax collector for a written balance before you sign the closing statement.

If you believe the assessment is too high, the Bergen County Board of Taxation at Two Bergen County Plaza in Hackensack hears appeals. The annual deadline is April 1, and the county's 2026 filing period has already passed. An owner of property assessed above $750,000 may file directly with the Tax Court by April 1 instead.

sections.h2: What does it cost to sell in Hackensack, and which forms do I sign?
sections.html:
The seller pays the state Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded. For a sale above $350,000 the schedule runs $2.90 per $500 on the first $150,000, $4.25 per $500 from $150,000 to $200,000, and $4.80 per $500 from $200,000 to $550,000, so a $400,000 sale comes to about $3,215. Prices over $1,000,000 also bring a graduated percent fee, with the schedule on the same state page.

  • Realty Transfer Fee, charged at recording.
  • The $70 Hackensack fire certificate fee.
  • Payoff of the mortgage and any recorded liens.
  • Your share of the current quarter's property tax.

A New Jersey resident seller signs the GIT/REP-3 residency certification so the clerk will accept the deed. A nonresident seller makes an estimated Gross Income Tax payment of at least 2 percent of the price unless an assurance on that form applies. Some transfers are exempt from the fee, including a deed from an executor to an heir named in the will.

sections.h2: What should a landlord know before selling a Hackensack rental?
sections.html:
About 63 percent of occupied Hackensack homes are rented, and the median gross rent is $1,911. The Department of Building, Housing and Land Use also serves as the administrative arm of the city's Rent Stabilization Board, so ask that office whether your building falls under rent stabilization before you set a price on market rents.

The state fire certificate applies to leases and changes of occupancy as well as sales, which means a tenant turnover and a sale can each call for an inspection. Schedule the inspection early so the certificate, valid for six months, covers the closing date.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit shape buyer interest in Hackensack?
sections.html:
Interstate 80, Route 17, Route 4 and County Route 503 serve the city, and the Court Street, Midtown and Anderson Street bridges cross the Hackensack River. The city counted 79.69 miles of roadway in 2010, with 62.10 maintained by the city, 15.10 by Bergen County and 2.49 by the state.

NJ Transit's Pascack Valley Line has two Hackensack stops, Anderson Street and Essex Street, with service to Hoboken and connections to Penn Station New York. Buses leave the Hackensack Bus Terminal for the Port Authority Bus Terminal and the George Washington Bridge Bus Station, and a listing that places the house near a station or the bus terminal speaks directly to commuters.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate to sell a house in Hackensack?
faqs.a: Yes, the state requires a smoke alarm certificate before a one-family or two-family house is sold, and Hackensack's Fire Prevention Bureau issues it. The city form also covers carbon monoxide alarms and a portable fire extinguisher, costs $70 and stays valid for six months.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer fee when I sell in Hackensack?
faqs.a: About $3,215 on a $400,000 sale, using the state's rate schedule for deals above $350,000. The seller pays it when the deed is recorded, and exemptions are limited to the cases the state lists, such as a deed between parent and child.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hackensack house that has unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but the balance has to be cleared at or before closing. Hackensack says taxes and charges must be current by November 10 to stay out of the accelerated tax sale that starts November 11, and interest builds at 8 percent on the first $1,500 and 18 percent beyond it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hackensack house with tenants living in it?
faqs.a: Yes, a house with tenants can be sold. Ask the Building, Housing and Land Use department whether rent stabilization applies, and have your attorney review each lease, because the buyer will inherit the occupancy.

faqs.q: What if I inherited a house in Hackensack?
faqs.a: An executor's deed to an heir named in the will is exempt from the Realty Transfer Fee, while a sale to an outside buyer is not. Either way, the estate completes a GIT/REP form based on its residency status, and Hackensack's fire certificate is still needed for a sale.
